Privacy Policy

How Hedley Ventures Ltd handles personal information.

Last updated: October 2026

Who we are

Hedley Ventures Ltd, company number SC896907, registered office 9 Ainslie Place, Edinburgh, Scotland, EH3 6AS, provides fractional CFO, strategic financial advisory and fundraising advisory services and operates this website. For the purposes of UK data protection law, Hedley Ventures Ltd is the controller of the personal information described in this policy.

This policy covers visitors to this website and the people we deal with in our work, including prospective and existing clients, founders, investors and other professional contacts.

If you have any questions about this policy or how we use your information, please contact us at thudson@hedleyventures.com.

Information we collect

Much of the information we hold is provided by you, for example when you contact us, meet us or work with us. If you contact us by email, or by using the enquiry form on our Contact page, we receive the details you provide. On the enquiry form this includes your name, email address and company name, the support you are interested in, your company’s approximate monthly revenue, any fundraising amount and timing you choose to share, and anything else you include in your message.

We also obtain business contact information from other sources, including professional networks such as LinkedIn, company websites, Companies House and other public sources, people who introduce us, and legitimate commercial providers of business contact information. This is usually limited to your name, role, organisation, business contact details and professional background, with notes of our dealings with you.

When we work with a client, the client may also share information about people connected with its business, such as directors, shareholders, employees and investors, where this is needed for the engagement.

Enquiries submitted through the form are stored securely in a private database so that we can respond to you and keep track of our conversation. Only Hedley Ventures can access this database, and access requires secure sign-in.

To protect the form against spam and abuse, we briefly keep a one-way, scrambled code derived from the IP address used to submit it, rather than the address itself. It is used only to limit repeated submissions and is deleted after two days.

Cookies, analytics and how you found us

This website does not use cookies, advertising or cross-site tracking. Our fonts and images are hosted on this website rather than loaded from third-party services.

We use Cloudflare Web Analytics, provided by Cloudflare, Inc., to understand how the website is used, for example how many visits it receives, which pages are viewed and which websites visitors arrive from. It does not use cookies, does not identify or follow individual visitors, and only provides us with combined figures.

So that we can understand which channels lead to enquiries, while you browse this website your browser temporarily remembers how your visit began: the first page you viewed, the website you came from (if any) and any campaign tags in the link you followed. This is kept only for the current browser tab and is cleared when you close it. It is sent to us only if you submit an enquiry, in which case it is stored with your enquiry. If you would prefer us not to keep this information, let us know and we will remove it.

To protect the enquiry form from spam, our Contact page uses Cloudflare Turnstile, a security check provided by Cloudflare, Inc. It may process technical information about your browser and device to confirm that the form is being completed by a person rather than an automated program. Further information is available in Cloudflare’s privacy policy.

Hosting and service providers

This website is hosted by GitHub Pages, a service provided by GitHub, Inc. When you visit the site, GitHub may automatically process technical information, such as your IP address, for the purposes of operating and securing its service. Further information is available in GitHub's privacy statement.

Enquiries submitted through the form are received and stored using services provided by Cloudflare, Inc., and notifications of new enquiries are delivered to us by Resend, an email delivery service. These providers process the information only to provide their services to us. Further information is available in Resend’s privacy policy.

To run our business more generally, we use established software providers, including Google Workspace for email, documents and records, and Xero for accounting and invoicing.

How we use your information

We use personal information to respond to enquiries, provide our services, identify potential clients and investors, maintain our professional relationships, send relevant business communications and keep business, accounting and tax records.

We rely on performing a contract with you, or taking steps at your request before entering into one; on complying with our legal obligations, such as accounting and tax requirements; and on our legitimate interests in running and developing our business, including building relationships with potential clients and investors and telling relevant business contacts about our work.

We may email people at companies and other incorporated organisations about our work without their prior consent. Each email will identify us and let you opt out. We only send marketing emails to sole traders and some partnerships with their consent, or where they have previously enquired about or used our services.

We do not sell your personal information or use it for automated decision-making.

Sharing your information

We share personal information with the service providers described above. In our advisory work, we may also share relevant information with investors, clients and other parties to a transaction (for example, when introducing a client to investors with the client’s agreement), and with our professional advisers. We will also share information where the law requires it.

Some of our service providers process information outside the UK, including in the United States. Where they do, the transfer is covered by UK adequacy regulations (such as the UK Extension to the EU–US Data Privacy Framework) or by contractual safeguards approved for transfers from the UK.

How long we keep your information

We keep website enquiries for up to 24 months after our last contact with you. If we go on to work together, we keep engagement records for as long as needed for that engagement and afterwards to meet legal, accounting, tax or insurance requirements and to deal with any questions or claims. We keep professional contact details for as long as they remain relevant to our work, and delete or update them when they are no longer needed. You can ask us to delete your information at any time, although we may need to keep some records where the law requires it.

Your rights

You have the right to request access to the personal information we hold about you, and to ask us to correct, delete or restrict the use of it. You may also object to our use of your information and, in some circumstances, ask us to transfer it to you or another organisation. To exercise any of these rights, please contact us using the details above.

You can object at any time to us using your information to send you business development communications. Just reply to any message from us or email us, and we will stop.

If you are unhappy with how we have handled your information, please contact us first so that we can look into it. We will acknowledge your complaint within 30 days and respond without undue delay. You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk).

Changes to this policy

We may update this policy from time to time. The latest version will always be available on this page.
